title: Seed lots
description: A lot, not a variety. The seed world certifies per lot: ISTA issues one certificate per lot, OECD's schemes label per lot, and a state certifying agency's determination attaches to a lot rather than to the variety it belongs to. The variety has its own record; this record says that THIS quantity of seed is of that variety, produced in that season by that grower, and tested with these results. The link to the variety is a parent, not a field, which is why this profile does not extend plant-variety/v1. Deliberately small: the fewer fields a certifying agency has to agree with us about, the more likely it adopts anything at all.

generationClass.description: The generation class this lot is offered as. These are the classes US certifying agencies work in, and they are a descent chain rather than four independent grades: certified descends from registered, registered from foundation, foundation from breeder. A record claiming a class without a parent lot of the class above it is claiming a generation it cannot show, which is exactly what the descent mechanism is for. `unclassified` is the honest value for seed produced outside a certification scheme.

productionYear.description: The year the lot was harvested. Two lots of the same variety from different seasons are different lots, never the same record corrected.

originCountry.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 of the country of production. Required by the OECD Seed Schemes for movement between participating countries, and the field a purchaser in another jurisdiction asks about first.

quantityKg.description: Weight of the lot as sealed. Recorded because a lot that has been split is a new lot with its own record, and the original quantity is what makes a split checkable.

germinationPercent.description: Germination as tested. Substantiate with an attestation from the testing laboratory: this profile records the claim, the attestation records who stands behind it.

purePercent.description: Pure seed fraction by weight. The complement is other crop seed, weed seed and inert matter; a purity analysis reports all four and the report hash carries the detail.

moisturePercent.description: Moisture content as tested. Determines whether stated germination survives storage, which is why a purchaser reads it alongside germination rather than after it.

seedTreatment.description: Chemical or biological treatment applied, as labelled. A treated lot and the same lot untreated are different lots.

sealedBy.description: The party that sealed the container, where sealing is what ISTA's rules make the lot a lot. Not the same as the holder of this record.

x-veilcore.extendsNote: Deliberately extends nothing. A seed lot is not a kind of variety, and inheriting breedingMethod or sportOrigin would put variety facts on a lot record where a certifying agency would rightly ask which one the determination attaches to.
x-veilcore.lotDesignation: Use the envelope's subject.internalDesignation for the lot designation, and the record identifier for the reference a third party resolves. ISTA requires a lot designation unique to its certificate; that is a rule about the issuer's practice, which the format records rather than enforces.
x-veilcore.parentRolesNote: `variety` points at the variety record this lot is of, and there is exactly one. `parent-lot` points at the lot of the class above, which is what a generation claim rests on. `blend-component` is for a lot assembled from several, where every component is a parent and none is the parent.
x-veilcore.provableFieldsNote: The fields a purchaser or an agency asks about as a threshold rather than a value: germination at or above a standard, moisture at or below one, a class in an accepted set. Numeric fields are scaled to integers because a proof system compares integers and 98.5 is not one; scale 10 means tenths of a percent, so 98.5 is committed as 985. Ordering here is the ordering of the content tree, and changing it produces a different schema.
x-veilcore.correctionSeverityNote: Test results are cosmetic for descent and material for terms, and the split is the point: a corrected germination figure does not change what the seed is, but it changes what a purchaser agreed to buy. Generation class, production year and country of origin are material for both, because each is a claim about where the lot came from rather than about how it performed.
